title: Reflexive modules extend across codimension two in a normal scheme
statement: Let $Y$ be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Suppose $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}\ge2$ for every $y\in Y\setminus V$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. A coherent module $F$ [pqf-def-coherent] is reflexive when the evaluation morphism $F\to\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(F,\mathcal O_Y),\mathcal O_Y)$ is an isomorphism [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Restriction and direct image [def-pc-module-pullback] give quasi-inverse equivalences between coherent reflexive modules on $Y$ and on $V$, with all module morphisms. Explicitly, for coherent reflexive $F$ on $Y$, the unit $F\to j_*(F|_V)$ is an isomorphism; for coherent reflexive $G$ on $V$, $j_*G$ is coherent reflexive and the counit $(j_*G)|_V\to G$ is an isomorphism. In particular restriction induces a bijection on every Hom set between coherent reflexive modules on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0EBJ (divisors-lemma-reflexive-S2-extend), specialized by the normal S2 criterion Tag 0345 (properties-lemma-criterion-normal).

proof.text: For $y\in Y\setminus V$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a normal domain by normality, and is Noetherian: take a Noetherian affine neighbourhood from the locally Noetherian cover and localize its ring at the prime of $y$. Localization preserves Noetherianity. Its dimension is at least two by hypothesis, so the normal-local-depth theorem gives $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{Y,y}\ge2$. These same local rings occur after restricting to any open neighbourhood of $y$.

source.place: Tag 0345 (properties-lemma-criterion-normal), S2 implication; Tag 0EBJ depth hypothesis.

proof.text: Open restriction preserves coherence by the coherence-locality theorem. It also preserves reflexivity: on an open $W\subseteq V$, the sections defining sheaf Hom are exactly the same module maps before and after restriction; hence restriction identifies the double dual and its evaluation map. Now let $F$ be coherent reflexive on $Y$. Write $F^\vee=\mathcal Hom(F,\mathcal O_Y)$. The structure module is quasi-coherent of finite type, hence coherent on this locally Noetherian scheme; coherent sheaf Hom shows $F^\vee$ is coherent. Thus $F^\vee$ is locally finitely presented and its stalks are finite. For a boundary point $y$, put $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $N=(F^\vee)_y$. The stalk-Hom comparison, applied with source $F^\vee$ and target $\mathcal O_Y$, identifies $(F^{\vee\vee})_y$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R)$. Evaluation identifies $F_y$ with this dual. Apply the existing local dual-depth theorem to the finite module $N$ and to the depth bound from step 1: $\operatorname{depth}_R F_y\ge2$. This is the stalk-depth argument of Tag 0EBI written from existing inputs. To check the Hartogs hypotheses, coherence gives quasi-coherence and finite type; the affine criterion gives finiteness on every affine open. The coherent local finite presentations also give finite stalks, by taking their cokernel at the point. Hartogs therefore gives the canonical unit isomorphism $\eta_F:F\xrightarrow{\sim}j_*(F|_V)$. This argument applies as well to any nonempty affine open of $Y$ with its intersection with $V$.

source.place: Tag 0EBJ (divisors-lemma-reflexive-S2-extend), first two sentences of proof; Tag 0EBI(1); Tag 0E9I.

proof.text: Let $G$ be coherent reflexive on $V$. Fix a nonempty affine open $A\subseteq Y$ and put $W=A\cap V$. The affine scheme $A$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Since an open immersion into a locally Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact, $W$ is quasi-compact. The coherent restriction $G|_W$ is of finite presentation by the local finite-presentation theorem. Apply the finite-presentation extension theorem with ambient module $0$ and zero map $G|_W\to0$: it gives a finitely presented $\mathcal O_A$-module $H$ and an isomorphism $H|_W\cong G|_W$. Finite presentation implies quasi-coherence and finite type. As $A$ is locally Noetherian, the coherent-finite-type criterion shows that $H$ is coherent. No global quasi-compactness of $Y$ or $V$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0EBJ proof, affine reduction and coherent extension; Tag 0G41(2) (properties-lemma-lift-finite-presentation), deduced from existing Tag 01PI with zero ambient module.

proof.text: On $A$, replace $H$ by the explicit double dual $E=H^{\vee\vee}$. The coherent-reflexive-hull lemma makes $E$ coherent reflexive. The sheaf-Hom formula on opens gives $E|_W=(H|_W)^{\vee\vee}\cong(G|_W)^{\vee\vee}\cong G|_W$, the last isomorphism being evaluation for $G|_W$. By step 2 applied on $A$, $E\cong (j_A)_*(E|_W)\cong (j_A)_*(G|_W)$, where $j_A:W\hookrightarrow A$. On an open $B\subseteq A$, both $((j_*G)|_A)(B)$ and $((j_A)_*(G|_W))(B)$ equal $G(B\cap V)$, with the same scalar action and restriction maps. Thus $(j_*G)|_A$ is coherent reflexive. Coherence is local on the affine cover, so $j_*G$ is coherent globally. Its stalk at each point is reflexive because it agrees on a neighbourhood with one of these coherent reflexive modules; the stalk criterion for reflexivity now proves $j_*G$ reflexive.

source.place: Tag 0EBJ proof, replace the extension by its reflexive hull and identify its pushforward; Tags 0AY4, 0AY3.

proof.text: For an open $B\subseteq V$, $((j_*G)|_V)(B)=G(B)$; the counit is the identity on these sections. It is therefore an isomorphism for every module $G$. Restriction and direct image act on every module morphism, and their units and counits are natural, so the preceding isomorphisms make these functors quasi-inverse on the stated full subcategories. Explicitly, if $F_1,F_2$ are coherent reflexive on $Y$ and $a:F_1|_V\to F_2|_V$, its extension is $\eta_{F_2}^{-1}\circ j_*a\circ\eta_{F_1}$. Its restriction equals $a$ since the restricted units are inverse to the counits. For any $b:F_1\to F_2$, naturality gives $\eta_{F_2}\circ b=j_*(b|_V)\circ\eta_{F_1}$; hence restriction is injective as well as surjective on Hom sets.

source.place: Tag 0EBJ conclusion; ordinary restriction/direct-image adjunction, with inverse on Hom sets written explicitly.

lean.statement: theorem normal_reflexive_open_equivalence {Y V : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (hnormal : ∀ y : Y, IsIntegrallyClosed (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) (j : V ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hcodim : ∀ y : Y, y ∉ Set.range j → (2 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) : (∀ F : Y.Modules, RingedSpace.IsCoherent Y.toRingedSpace F → IsIso (SheafOfModules.bidual (R := Y.sheaf) F) → RingedSpace.IsCoherent V.toRingedSpace ((restrictFunctor j).obj F) ∧ IsIso (SheafOfModules.bidual (R := V.sheaf) ((restrictFunctor j).obj F)) ∧ IsIso ((restrictAdjunction j).unit.app F)) ∧ (∀ G : V.Modules, RingedSpace.IsCoherent V.toRingedSpace G → IsIso (SheafOfModules.bidual (R := V.sheaf) G) → RingedSpace.IsCoherent Y.toRingedSpace ((pushforward j).obj G) ∧ IsIso (SheafOfModules.bidual (R := Y.sheaf) ((pushforward j).obj G)) ∧ IsIso ((restrictAdjunction j).counit.app G)) ∧ (∀ F₁ F₂ : Y.Modules, RingedSpace.IsCoherent Y.toRingedSpace F₁ → IsIso (SheafOfModules.bidual (R := Y.sheaf) F₁) → RingedSpace.IsCoherent Y.toRingedSpace F₂ → IsIso (SheafOfModules.bidual (R := Y.sheaf) F₂) → Function.Bijective (fun f : F₁ ⟶ F₂ ↦ (restrictFunctor j).map f))
lean.note: The equivalence is stated in its canonical adjunction form: restriction and direct image preserve coherent reflexive modules, the restricted unit and counit are isomorphisms, and the actual restriction map on all Hom sets is bijective. Reflexivity uses the existing SheafOfModules.bidual evaluation, without a new predicate or an arbitrary double-dual isomorphism.
